utterances.text: And can you tell us, in general terms, what your responsibilities were or what the nature of your involvement was and is with respect to that project?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My -- the purpose of this -- or my involvement was in respect to the updates on the -- on the current number of the identified individuals regarding the Srebrenica-related events, as well as to the exhumations which were conducted between -- in these periods, because the exhumations regarding Srebrenica events are ongoing process in Bosnia, and every year they exhumed additional graves and found victims from Srebrenica events. So in -- I was involved in gathering information on these exhumations. I was involved in -- in having contacts with BH authorities, ICMP, and with the people on the ground in Bosnia, so in order to get as many information and new evidence on these graves which were exhumed after 2001, when the ICTY completed their exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Just a moment ago, you mentioned a Dean Manning. Can you just tell us who that is in relation to what you're doing now concerning this investigation?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dean Manning was investigator for the OTP. I think he left the Tribunal around 2003, and he was dealing with the same issue before. And he prepared several reports in respect to the exhumations, which were done by the ICTY and later on by the BiH authorities. And he also testified in several cases. And my report is just updating his previous reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that one of your functions was the gathering of information. Could you just tell us, as briefly as possible, what kinds of information or materials, generally, were you involved in gathering or reviewing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I briefly already mentioned that we were -- I was gathering the information on the specific grave-sites which were exhumed by the BiH and are related to Srebrenica events. So those would be exhumation records, exhumation -- yeah, exhumation records, where you can get information on, for example, when a certain exhumation site was exhumed, how many bodies were found in it, and what kind of evidence were found during the exhumation. So, yeah, these were basic things which -- in respect to -- to get information on these graves. Also, not only on the graves; as we will speak later on, I was also involved in getting information on the surface remains which were found in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how would you describe the nature of the investigation and your involvement in reviewing or determining the number of Srebrenica and Zepa-related victims? Is that a straightforward thing, is it a short-term thing, or --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's a long-term process, because these exhumations started in 1996 and are still ongoing. It's an ongoing process. Every day, there are new identifications of the victims which were already exhumed from these graves by the ICMP, and also there are -- there are ongoing exhumations on a daily basis. So, yeah, it's a long-term process, so that's why we have to be in contact with the BiH authorities every day to see what is going on on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you mentioned a report updating -- you mentioned a report updating some of Dean Manning's work. Have you prepared -- how many reports have you prepared in connection with this responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection to this responsibility, I prepared three reports. This is my third report. Actually, the first report was prepared in March 2009, and then in April 2009 I prepared a corrigendum to that report. In August 2009, I prepared an additional report which was called "Addendum," actually for Perisic team. And this is my latest report from April 2010 which I prepared for this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to your preparation of these reports, did you receive any assistance in putting them together?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regard to assistance, yes. I received the assistance from the -- from our analyst, Panayota Vassou, who was dealing mainly with DNA connections, in co-operation with me. But the rest is more or less -- yeah, it's my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was your report prepared independently?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you, if we could -- I'd just like to focus you on your newest report. You indicated that that was a 21 April 2010 report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the purpose and objective of that report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose and objectives of these -- of this report were to basically present to the Trial Chamber the current number of the identified individuals from the -- related to the Srebrenica event. Also, the purpose was to highlight how many -- how many graves have been exhumed so far, when they were exhumed. Then there is a section of surface remains, so to present to the Trial Chamber how many of them have been so far identified and found on the ground. And, of course, to present the new forensic evidence which emerged recently. So I'm referring here specifically to DNA connections between the graves, which shows which points, actually -- which primary graves and secondary graves are related to each other. Also, in relation to my report, there were instances where we can now link, for example, the evidence which were already obtained during the site visits or crime scene investigations back in 1996. I am specifically referring here to Kravica warehouse and Pilica, where certain identification documents were found at these places. And now when we have -- when the individuals from the graves were found, we can see that there is a link between these primary graves to certain secondary graves. So these are the main purposes of this update.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does your report follow on, and that is this particular report, does it follow on in terms of updating Mr. Manning's report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a follow-up of Dean Manning's report and also of my previous report from 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you've indicated that it relates to the events -- Srebrenica events. Does it account for anything related to the events in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This is new in this report, the chapter about Zepa. Actually, I am referring this new report also to the victims of Zepa-related events, so there we have one grave and several surface remains in relation to these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does your report account for any new mass graves or other graves that are related to either Srebrenica or Zepa? Since your last report, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, there are certain graves which were not part of my previous report, and that's simply because they were exhumed recently, last year. And we have already identifications -- positive identifications from these graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does your new report in any way relate to evidence that were obtained during crime scene investigations of various grave-sites and so on related to Srebrenica or Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that I already mentioned that, that there are evidence which were found during the crime scene investigations, in particular these IDs, and then we can link them to particular -- to certain secondary graves or primary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that you relied on a number of sources in preparing your report. Could you tell us what the main sources were for preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The main source was the ICMP -- what the ICMP match reports which were sent in February 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just ask you to clarify so that we're all clear. What is the ICMP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The ICMP stands for the International Commission on Missing Persons, which is stationed or based in Sarajevo, and they are dealing with the missing persons and identifications of the victims from Bosnia -- missing persons from Bosnia. And the main source was the update, because every few months we are getting the updates from their side on the identifications of the victims from Srebrenica. So the latest one was from February, and this was the main source which I used in my report to present the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what kind of identifications are you referring to, in particular?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the identifications of the victims which were -- which were killed or murdered or -- after the -- or during the -- during the take-over or after the take-over of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yeah. In particular, I'm referring to your reference to a match report. What are we talking about when you say "match report"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I used, in my report, the identification, although the correct -- the correct phrase would be "DNA matching report," as it is used by the ICMP. It means that the DNA sample which was taken from the human remains found in the graves have been matched to the blood donors, which were given to the ICMP by the relatives -- from the relatives of these victims. So it means that a particular individual, a DNA sample was matched to that donor. So it means it is an identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So we're talking about DNA identification.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, we are all the time talking about the DNA identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you refer to any other ICMP reports, such as summary reports, or field notes, or things of that nature?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I also referred to the ICMP summary reports for -- I can tell you that ICMP participated in these exhumations, especially of the largest secondary and -- secondary graves, and they participated with their experts, archaeologists. And after the completion of the exhumations, they have -- they have generated the reports about these particular sites. And, yes, these reports -- I reviewed these reports, and I also noted them in my -- in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: These reports -- just so we're clear on the record, when you say "these reports," are you referring to summary reports, or are you referring to field notes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I'm referring to both. We received for certain sites, I think for four of the secondary graves, only field notes from their site because they have not generated any other report. So -- but these field notes are in handwritten version, so what I have been particularly referring to are the ICMP summary reports which are written and generated by them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the summary reports and field notes, are those notes or reports related to DNA identifications, or are they related to other types of forensic analysis?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, those reports are not related to DNA identifications, but they are related to the actual exhumations, itself, how they were conducted, what kind of evidence were found there inside these graves, and what are their conclusions, especially from the archaeological point of view. They're saying or writing down their findings and conclusions about if it is a secondary grave; for example, we have one mixed grave and we have one robbed grave. And all those facts are noted during the exhumations and are part of their reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you consider sources of information, besides the ICMP, in preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Beside the ICMP records, I also considered other sources. Mainly, these were documents received by the Tuzla and Sarajevo Cantonal Prosecutor's Office, and those were received upon our request for assistance from the BiH authorities. Apart from that, some documents on these exhumations were also provided to us by the BiH State Prosecutor's Office, and also we have been -- I have been in contact with the BiH Federal Commission on Missing Persons, which has now remained into the BiH Institute on Missing Persons. So these are the main other sources I have also used in order to compile my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you review or consider any other DNA records relative to the number of individuals associated with the events in Srebrenica and Zepa to account for that number? From any source other than ICMP, I should add.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. There were several individuals which were identified already before ICMP commenced its work in 2001. In November in 2001, they have started with DNA identifications. Before that, there were several individuals already identified, and those individuals are part of Dean Manning's report. And for my report, I also included those individuals in total numbers. And these individuals who were identified by the PHR, which means Physicians for Human Rights, and ICRC, which stands for International Commission on the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the process by which the ICMP carries out DNA identifications, in general terms?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in general terms, I am familiar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you just describe that a little bit for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I'm familiar how -- how -- what is the process in order to get the DNA sample from them after the autopsy have been conducted, so -- and then basically this DNA sample is tested by them. And if it is matched to the blood donors, then it is -- their report about this DNA positive match is generated. And this positive identification is then entered into their -- into their database, and a list of which is sent regularly to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll talk a little bit about this later, but what kinds of samples, if you know, are tested and matched against blood donor samples, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the samples which are taken during the autopsy from the human remains of the bodies found within the grave, and these samples are usually the samples where the possibility of the -- positive DNA identification is very high. So I would say they are taking usually the teeth, and then the long bones, like it is femur and other bones, and these are basically the samples which are taken during the autopsy. And then these samples are sent to the ICMP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the preparation of your report, are these the types of documents that you used in order to prepare it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, these are the types of report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are the sources for most of the information that you considered in preparing your report identified or referenced in the report, itself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct, they are all -- they are all referenced in my report. So every single conclusion I made, it is based on certain reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how are they indicated? Are they indicated by title, author?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually, I refer them as a report, and then beside that I put down the ERN number of the actual report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the material that you've referenced in your report, did you review all that material?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I reviewed this material, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, did you make any attempt or effort to try and verify the accuracy of the information of the reports on which you relied in preparing your own report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's a constant duty, and I am doing -- doing that. And I can say that, indeed, I have been checking the reliability of those reports. Especially, I can say for certain individuals, during the analysis of this ICMP data, there were some typo -- for example, typo mistakes found in this data. So according to our findings, we assume they are typos, and then we informed the ICMP in order to point it out. So then it's up to them to accept this as being typos or not. So, yeah, there are contacts in order -- with the ICMP is if we have any kind of questions or doubts regarding this ICMP data, so we are asking them for clarifications to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you have any contacts -- I'm sorry. You actually indicated that you had some contacts with the Bosnian authorities with respect to exhumation data. And was that -- is that a continuous thing, or is that something that has happened only occasionally? If you could just describe that for us.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are regular contacts with them, so through the requests of -- for the assistant -- assistance, we are sending this request to them in order to get documents. Then apart from that, we have -- I mean, personally I have regular telephone contacts, especially with the BiH Institute on Missing Persons. And we have also contacts with the ICMP through e-mails, so sometimes we exchange some e-mails in order to get information or clarifications from them. So in order to be updated, I am having regular contacts with BiH authorities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you rely on any expert reports in preparing your updated report in April 2010?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because those were mostly -- mostly summarised by Dean Manning in his report, and my report, itself, should be read in conjunction with his previous reports, where he's referring to these expert reports. But in order to make certain conclusions about the connections between these sites, I reviewed those reports, and I am considering them as relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to these reports that you did consider, aside from the expert reports that were evaluated by Dean Manning, can you tell us, generally, how you received the materials that you reviewed and that you've referenced in your report? Did you receive them directly or indirectly? Are they from the source or from a secondary source? If you could just explain that to the Trial Chamber, I think that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there is a -- the RFA, request for assistance, sent to the authorities, then the documentation and everything what was requested is sent back to us in a normal -- normal way, diplomatic mail. And apart from that, I already mentioned that we exchanged some e-mails with the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina and also the ICMP, and this -- these are the ways how we are obtaining the documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the documentation that you received, do you have any concerns or questions about its authenticity as derived from the sources from whom you requested it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For these documents, no, because they are provided to us by the -- by the authorities of the BiH, and I don't think there is any question of their authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of the extent of your reliance on the information that we've spoken about concerning your report, could you tell us, for different parts of your report, for example, in terms of the DNA connections, what documents you predominantly relied upon? Is that the ICMP data that you referred to before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, this is predominantly is the ICMP data, what I relied upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of your analysis of the grave-sites, themselves, and the exhumation data, which documents did you predominantly rely upon in generating your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to get information on the actual exhumation site, when it was exhumed, by whom was it exhumed, what site code was designated to a particular grave, these kind of information I'm getting from the exhumation records which are generated by the authorities -- BiH authorities during the exhumation or immediately after it, and also, along with the exhumation records, the autopsy reports on every single individual which is found in these graves were provided to us, and these were also taken into consideration. Apart from that, there are also exhumation photographs, autopsy photographs, sketches. So all these documents are important -- were important for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you were made aware of certain new graves that you've included in the preparation of your report. Could you tell us what those were.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, there were certain graves which were exhumed after I generated my previous report in 2009, so the -- in July 1992 -- 2009, sorry, there was exhumation conducted of the Cancari Road 1 grave. So and this is the last -- the last grave which was known to the ICTY before which was exhumed. So all the graves which were known to the ICTY are now exhumed, but not all of the bodies which were exhumed from these graves are processed already. So it means we'll have, for Cancari 1, and I know for Cancari 8, we have no identifications yet from these exhumations. So apart from that, there were several additional exhumations conducted in 2009. One of those is in Mehurici village, which is close to Vlasenica. That one was done in May 2001. And because we have already positive identifications of the victims -- of the Srebrenica victims in these graves, this site is part of my report. In addition, there were also exhumations -- another one in Bisina area. That was Bisina Kev [phoen] exhumation, and an additional exhumation in -- I think the place is called Zaledje, which is near Srebrenica. According to the BiH, there might be the victims from Srebrenica. But since we don't have any confirmation yet on the actual identifications, none -- no people from these graves were already identified, so we cannot conclude if they are indeed Srebrenica related. And when we get this information, I will include this -- if they are Srebrenica-related victims into my new update.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you, if I could in e-court, 65 ter 5754A. All right, Mr. Janc. Do you recognise what's in front of you in e-court?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And what I'd like to do is to just go over, generally, the organisation of your report. If you could explain for the Trial Chamber, just in general terms, how it's -- how it's organised. And if we could go to the second page, I think, in both documents, that might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can explain. As you can see, this is the first page of my report, which is actually six pages' long. And then I have four annexes to this report in order to support my findings there, so annex A, annex B, annex C, and confidential annex D.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If you could just start with annex A and tell us, generally, what that's about.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Annex A refers to the actual exhumations of the graves, when they were conducted, by whom, and it points out also to the individuals which were exhumed -- how much individuals have been identified, not exhumed, identified so far per individual, per certain grave. So annex A refers to graves exhumed in relation to Srebrenica victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to annex B, if you could tell us briefly what that concerns.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Annex B relates to surface remains, so it is my summary of the surface remains analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, well, we'll get into a little more detail with that. But can you just tell us, generally, when you say "surface remains," what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the -- I'm referring -- when I say "surface remains," certain individuals were killed during the combat or also -- also during -- after the fall of Srebrenica, the column -- the column passed through Konjevic Polje towards -- to the north to Zvornik, and certain individuals were killed there, so -- and they were never buried, and, as such, were found -- their remains were found during those years from 1995 up to now. There are still exhumations of these people -- of these individuals. They were never buried, and they were just left on the ground. And these are the individuals which I referred as surface remains, and bodies of which -- remains of which just left -- left on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to annex C, can you tell us what that concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, is it possible to have the first page of the annex on the screen so that we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm actually going to go through each one of them individually, if that's all right with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's fine. That we can do after the second break.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You were going to put the last question to the witness. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If you could just tell us briefly, what does annex C concern?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Annex C concerns to the DNA connections, to the analysis of the DNA connections which were established regarding the ICMP data. So it relates to the connections between the graves, itself. And when we'll go into that section, we'll -- I'll explain a little bit more what that -- what it consists of and how we made certain conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And concerning annex -- confidential annex D, can you tell us what that's about.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Confidential annex D consists of the individuals. It is actually the list of the individuals which support the numbers which we will see on the second page of my report. There are only numbers summarised in my report, how many -- how many individuals were found in certain graves or in certain locations. And in annex D, you will find the actual names of these individuals. So they are the lists of the individuals which I'm referring in my reports just as the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. President, I'm not -- I wasn't sure if you were suggesting that it was the break time. Is that -- is that right? I'm sorry, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I think it is a convenient time for everybody now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, that's perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: A half hour. We will have our second break now, for technical reasons, and we resume at 10 minutes before 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Do we still have 5754A in e-court? We don't. If we could please go to page 2 in both documents. All right, thank you. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you can see there, in your report, that's written in bold: "Srebrenica and Zepa victims identified via DNA and other analysis in graves." And you've indicated a figure of 5.777. If we could go to the next page, please, in the English, I believe, in the B/C/S as well. Now, with respect to the figure, 5.777, could you tell us, first, what that represents? And then we'll take a look at this chart and you can explain a little bit about that. What does the figure 5.777 represent?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This figure represents the current number of the identified individuals which were found in the graves and are related to -- and are Srebrenica victims. So the total number now is 5.777 victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could now take a look at the chart that you have in front of you. I think we may have to go to the next page, page 4, for the B/C/S. Okay. Actually, I think the heading -- the headings that I want to review with you are on the previous page in the B/C/S, so if we could go back to page 3 just so that we see the headings, I think, yeah, and then we can go over those in the English. On the left-most column in the English, you can see "Mass grave." Can you tell us what these headings are. If you could explain that to the Trial Chamber. When you say "mass grave," what do you mean by that, first?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is the first column, and it should be -- it should be written "Graves," not "Mass Graves." So here is a mistake, because what is presented here in this table, and we'll see it on the following page, these are all the graves. And why I'm saying not only mass graves, because also the individual graves are included in this counting. So the last 11 entries, not on this page but on the page following this, will be the individuals -- individual graves. So -- and the other graves are the graves where more than one individuals were found. That's why it should be written "Graves." And these are the names of the sites where these exhumations took place, so -- and the sites as -- yeah, as were designated during the exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "these are the names of the sites," to what are you referring to? You're referring to the names under "Mass Graves," or the designations under "Site Code"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we are still at the first column. So I'm referring to these -- let's start with Cerska. And you can see some of them are bolded ones, so those bolded ones were exhumed by the ICTY. Wherever you see the bolded grave-site, those were exhumed by the ICTY. The others which were not bolded were exhumed by the BiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. To be --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And just one small correction, because in total number of 5.777 are included also the individuals which are related to Zepa events, so those 80 individuals which are -- which were found exhumed from Glogova [phoen] grave. So only one grave you can see inside this table in front of us is related to Zepa. The others are related to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And if we could go to the next column, and tell us what is indicated there under "Site Code." And let's stick with Cerska, because on the B/C/S version that's all that's indicated on the page under the headings.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the exhumation -- or before the exhumation, each site is assigned with a particular site code just in order to easily -- this site is easily referred in the future, so -- and it usually consists of the letters and the numbers. As you can see for Cerska site, the designated site code was "CSK" by the ICTY. And then if you go down, for example, we have here "Cincari Road 6," I will take the example for 6, and then we have in brackets "Kamenica 6."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just a moment. I think we have to change the page in the B/C/S, and that will be page 4. Just so that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt shortly to make something clear. In the transcript, page 69, line 19 to 23, you were referring to a number of 80 individuals related to Zepa. Could you please indicate in which column and in which line we will find it in this table.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, no problem. It is most probably a mistake, because it's not 80, but eight individuals. So -- and it is for Vragolovi grave. If you go to another page, one page after this one, we'll find the Vragolovi grave after the first column -- under the first column.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's on the second-to-last page on the English, and that's, I think, page 5 in the English -- 5 in the B/C/S. In the English, I believe it's page 5 as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can't see it on the English version. Okay, here it is, yes. Now, you can see Vragolovi site. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's about seven --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight from the top. So Vragolovi. "VRG" is the site code and when it was exhumed, and then the last column, it says how many individuals have been identified so far from this site. So it's eight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Only these eight that have a relation to Zepa or others to Srebrenica. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to clarify because of the figure. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We were talking about the site codes --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I wanted to explain the thing with -- if you can go back to page number 3, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. It's page 3 in the English, and we'll stay with page 4 in the B/C/S. Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I took an example of Cancari road number 6, for example, and you can see for many other sites, and I explain why there is something in brackets which is some written differently than from the other part of it. Cancari Road 6 was initially -- initially found as a secondary grave by the ICTY, and it was not exhumed by the ICTY, but it was handed over to the BiH authorities. When they have done this exhumation in 2008, and this is the information you can get in the third column, when the actual exhumation took place, they designated this site with a different code and also with a different name. So they renamed the actual site. And in order to stay consistent with our -- with our designations, because we are always referring to the same numbers and to the same site codes, I am putting this site in brackets. In brackets, it means what was designated by the BiH site, and we will find, in all the exhumation records and all the -- in this ICMP data, we'll find this site code as a reference to this particular site. So if it says "KAM06ZVO," it will be referring to Cancari 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If you could just explain for us, for example, these site codes, in some instances you'll see that the designation, for example, "PLC," and that's -- we're about five down from the top of this document, following "Orahovac." You can see the designation "PLC" for the site code, but the grave is indicated as "Branjevo Military Farm." Can you explain why that designation is a bit different from the name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is up to the exhumation team, who decide what kind of site code will be designated to particular exhumation site. So I'm not sure why they have decided at that time that for this site designation or site code would be "PLC" instead of something else, but they have just decided that, and that's how it is today. And whenever we see this site code, we know that this is related to Branjevo Military Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is Branjevo Military Farm associated with Pilica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. We have confirmation that bodies from Pilica Cultural Dom which were killed there during the execution were buried initially at the Branjevo Military Farm burial site.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And the next column indicates the exhumation date. And from what information is that derived?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is exhumation data for the ICTY exhumed graves. We know when they were exhumed because we exhumed them. And for the BiH-exhumed graves, these information are derived from the exhumation records, as well as the site codes and the site name, and all this information are derived from there. I'm getting the information from this documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on the far right, you have a column indicated "Identified Individuals, March 2009 - February 2010." Just tell us generally what that means, and then I'll put a couple of questions to you in respect to it.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, the first column under "Identified Individuals," which has "March 2010 --" "2009," sorry, it comes out of my previous report from March 2009. So these were the numbers of the identified individuals at that time. So the last column, which says "February 2010," there are the numbers of the individuals identified so far. So I wanted to present the increment in the numbers, that you can see how these numbers are growing, and the process is still ongoing. And we'll see for some sites -- for example, we can see here for Cancari Road 6, if you take this example, no individuals were identified at that time. I add because, as you can see, they are exhumed between October and December in 2008. And when I generated my report in March 2009, there were no individuals identified at that time yet. But now, one year after that, we have 158 individuals already identified from that site.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we can just page down, I think, in the B/C/S. No, we'll have to go to the next page in the B/C/S and also the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what I would like to do is to focus you or direct you to the grave-site Liplje 2. That's a bolded designation, and I think it's about -- well, about a third of the way down from the top. Now, in that case you can see the numbers for 2009 are indicated 174, and then in 2010, the numbers indicate 173, meaning one less individual associated or recovered from that grave. Can you explain why or how that would be the case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is the site designated as LP02, exhumed by the ICTY. When I have been checking on this issue, I came to the conclusion that the ICMP in the meantime re-labelled one of the individuals which was before -- allegedly found in Liplje 2 to Lazete 2, so he was re-labelled. According to them, it must be mistake before -- in labelling. So they re-labelled that individual into the Lazete 2 site, so that same individual will now appear there, is counted there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we can go to the next page, please, in the English and the B/C/S. Okay. And what I want to do is I want to talk about these numbers that you have indicated at the bottom. All right. And we have Srebrenica and Zepa graves total, for 2009, 5.275, and for 2010, 5.777. Okay. And with respect to the following row, can you tell us, Srebrenica and Zepa surface remains, 648 in 2009 and 703 in 2010, can you tell us a little bit about that. First tell us what you mean when you say "surface remains."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already explained before what I meant with "surface remains," and I have to a little bit clarify. I meant -- I testified before that these are only the victims -- the combat victims, which is not totally true, because we know there were also others which committed suicides, which were killed when crossing the minefields, or some of them were even killed. We know of them for one particular site, that they were killed not in combat. And these are the ones which were actually found on the surface, and the number -- the total number of those identified individuals in 2009 was 648 -- 48, yes. And now it's 703. And for the graves above that, we have -- you also can you also can see the increment. So 5.777 is the total number of all the graves you can see in this table above that number. So it's a total -- it's a total number, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, that total number of 703, does that account for all of the -- all of the, shall we say, victims that were recovered from the surface or identified from the surface?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them, because many of the surface remains have still not been identified or will never be identified because they were at such state of -- at such state, after so many years being exposed to weather conditions, that according to the ICMP, it will never be possible to identify all of them. So these are just the individuals which have been identified from these surface remains. But in total, there have been, you know -- because usually they are counting cases, how many cases have been collected from the surface, and I think it's roughly around 950 cases in total so far collected from the surface. So -- but we cannot make any conclusion how many of them have been identified or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you say that you have 950, approximately, surface remains, and all of those, only 703 are identified, how is it that you're able to determine that there are 950? Is that through DNA analysis, or anthropological analysis, or some other means of counting those individuals?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is everything -- not all of them, but most of them, because we have 35 individuals identified before the ICMP in 2000 -- in 2001, but most of them you can find on the ICMP data, based on their, again, site codes, and everything we received from the BiH Commission on Missing Persons. So not all of them have been identified so far, 950 cases. But one case, it doesn't mean one person. One case is such -- it can be many individuals or several cases can be only one individual, so it is just -- it's difficult to assess how many of them have been identified. But I have -- I have made a rough statistical examination of this issue, and I came to the conclusion that 1.1 case, roughly, is needed for one individual to be identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. When you say "a case," as distinguished from an individual, could you just explain how you come to that? How would you define a case in that circumstance?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, for example, you have that many -- it would be better if you go into surface remains section, that I can discuss, or we can discuss it later, because it will be easier to explain what the case means and how did I come to that conclusion. That I can show you on examples, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. We can get into that a little bit later. Let's go to the next row, which concerns others Serbia-related, Kozluk surface, Godinjske Bare, and uncategorised. If you could explain to the Trial Chamber what that refers to.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These four categories of identified individuals, I made it separately somehow because of the certain -- of certain facts. For example, we have Serbia-related victims. Those, I think 18 of them, individuals have been found along the Drina in Sava River on Serbian side in 1995. So they were taken out from the river and later on buried somewhere in Serbia, and re-exhumed in the beginning of 2000 -- 2001, something like that, by the Serbian side, and then samples taken from these individuals and tested in Bosnia and being identified as Srebrenica-related victims. So then we have another part is Kozluk surface, so those are individuals which are found very close to the Kozluk execution site, on the Drina River bank. And I -- based on how they were found, you cannot conclude -- and based on the documentation we have received on this exhumation site, I was not able to conclude that these are, indeed, surface remains, because I would -- my assumption would be -- and conclusion, that they were buried initially, but because of the -- of the Drina River and because they were exposed to the -- they were very close buried to Drina River, and I think they were just -- they just came on a surface because of the natural cause. So that's why I place them there. And there we have Godinjske Bare. Godinjske Bare are the individuals which were killed, and we have a video on these killings and are referred in the indictment as the -- sorry, I forgot it. It's no killing -- these are the individuals which are killed there. Although found on our surface, we know that they were killed. And then we have the last section there, uncategorised sites. So we have requested the documentation from the BiH authorities for all the site codes, all the sites which they exhumed. And based on the documentation we received, I am unable -- or I cannot say if the individuals found in these graves or in these sites, within these sites, are the actual graves or surface remains, so I cannot categorise them. So I think it is -- there is 39 of such individuals which are Srebrenica victims, but we can just not say if they were found on the surface or they were in graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, we'll get into those a little bit -- just a little bit in more detail when we get to the section concerning surface remains, but what I'd like to focus you on now is a little bit about your methodology in reaching the numbers that we've just gone over. I'd like to put before you 65 ter 6268, please. And I think we should not broadcast this.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I think we should have into -- into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm told that this number can't be correct. We don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We're checking now, but I think Ms. Stewart's indicated that she's able to get it. So let me just double-check the number. I apologise. I understand the number is right. Maybe we can try again and see if it will come up. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is this perhaps document --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's there, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yeah, that would be useful to rotate it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Janc. Are you -- well, it's a bit small now, but are you able to see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's still too small. But I know what is where, so I can -- I can comment on it. But I think it's better that we make it a little bit bigger. We'll start from the left-hand side first, and then we'll go -- we'll move towards the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Are you able to see that now a little bit more clearly, or would you like it blown up more?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's fine, it's fine with me. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Could you first explain or tell us what this is. And then explain how it relates to the methodology that you employed in developing your report.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is actual -- these are actual data which I was referring as ICMP data. So the actual spreadsheet which is obtained by -- obtained from the ICMP, which is provided by them to the ICTY. So when you open -- this is the first page. I have made an example. When you open that Excel spread sheet, you know, these are the first 30 entries you can see on their spreadsheet. So -- and they are -- this spreadsheet is in alphabetical order by the first column, where it says "MP," and it means "Missing Person." So you can see the name of the individuals which were matched to the -- to the donors. And you would see the last name of the individual. Then in the brackets there is a father name of the individual, and there is a first name at the end. The second column relates to the data of birth of that individual. Then we have a protocol ID, which refers to DNA -- a DNA sample. So protocol -- one protocol ID would always refer to one DNA sample and, consequently, to one individual. So -- and this protocol ID was very important when we have been analysing the DNA connections, and we'll come to that later and I will explain why are these so important.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you for a second. When you say that one protocol ID relates to one DNA sample, are you talking about the sample of DNA from the missing persons or the sample of DNA obtained from the donor?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it relates to a DNA sample of the missing -- of a missing person. But I don't -- I don't mean to -- only one sample, but the same sample of -- it can be several samples. We'll see it later, that we have, for example, for one individual several samples have been tested and matched to one individual. So all these several multiple samples will get the unique protocol ID number which will always refer to one DNA. It means to one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We can go to the next column.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. The next column is "Case ID," and here we can find -- or we can see where the individual was found. So this "Case ID" consists of several letters and numbers, and the first part of the entry refers to a site, to a particular exhumation site, and here you can find the actual site codes, what we have been discussing before. So, for example, if you go to the first entry, I think it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could blow that up, I think it would be better for everybody to see. Maybe even a little bit bigger. That would be helpful. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. If you go to the first entry, we can see that it says "KAM10ZVO." So this is a reference to a particular exhumation site. So in this case, it is Cancari 10. So when I see this designation, I immediately know that this particular body or body parts were found in this Cancari 10 grave. So -- and this important in order to establish which -- which of these cases were found where, and this was important for my analysis to conclude -- to put the certain individuals from this -- from this data into certain -- into particular grave-sites. So -- and then in addition, we have numbers. After "ZVO," we see it is 1, 3, and something else. It's 1330, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This number refers to a body or body part which was designated to this particular body during the exhumation. So it means this refers to a body part number 1339 during the exhumation. But in this case, where we see "T" at the end, it also means something. "T" would stand for "Tijelo" in B/C/S, which means a body, so it means a body was found and designated as such. And then we have the last part of this entry, which says "LF," and I have to explain a little bit more. Now, I have been referring that this is a body found there. But what we see here under the "Case ID" is actually the label which was sent together with the DNA sample from the pathologist to the ICMP. So -- but this pathologist have taken the sample from the body, 1338, and sent this sample to the ICMP. And also what it is at the end, "LF," it means that this sample was taken, I think, from left femur of this particular body.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to the next column, we see "ID ICMP." And tell us what that means.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the identification number of the individuals which are on the missing person and identified -- which are on the ICMP missing list, on the list they created themselves, and they assigned a particular number for every single individual. So this is actually the number for every particular individual has its own identification number. So these are the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is it ever the case that more than one ID ICMP corresponds to a protocol ID or a single protocol ID?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have such cases, and we'll see such cases during my testimony. There, we will have situations, cases, where we will have several ID numbers listed here under one protocol ID; two or even more. So this is the case when the ICMP was unable to match the particular individual to DNA donors. Actually, when we are -- when they have -- when there are sibling cases, for example, when there are two brothers, it is sometimes difficult to then distinguish which of two brothers was identified. They know that this particular individual is son of someone who is a donor, but they don't know who of those two brothers, which are both missing, is who. So they can find for both brothers, and they will find for both brothers the unique DNA profile, but they will not be able to say who is who of those two brothers. They would both have -- for example, the protocol ID for both brothers will be different, but they will not be able to connect this brother to a particular site.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know why that is the case or how it could be that if each person has a unique DNA profile, you might have a situation where you can't distinguish between brothers as they relate to a single DNA profile?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are situations, and I think it's more a scientific question. But I know that sometimes they don't have enough donors in order to conclude who of two brothers or of three brothers was found where. They will find three different DNA samples, for each and every single one, but they will not be able to link them -- they will not be able to distinguish between them, so they will not be able to say which of those three brothers was found where. They will just know that all three have been identified. But who of them was identified in which site, they will not be able to say. And in this case, we'll see, under "ID ICMP," two or three numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could go over to the -- well, the next column, we can see that's the site name, which is indicated. I don't think we need to go over that. We have the site coordinates.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, site name and site coordinates relates to the exhumation site, so how is it called, the exhumation site, itself, and where it is located in the area. So these are GPS coordinates of the site coordinates, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then we have "Jurisdiction."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this is jurisdiction which they put, for example -- for most of the cases, we'll have "BiH Federation Commission," under which jurisdiction these individuals are -- these missing persons have been exhumed. And, for example, for Serbia-related, we'll see a different jurisdiction. It is "Serbia" listed as jurisdiction, as jurisdiction, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then we have "Date of Submission."

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Date of Submission," for this one I'm not sure if it is date of the submission of the DNA sample to the ICMP, or it is date of submission of the actual -- of the actual report which was generated by the ICMP already, based on the positive identification. So either of those two, this is the case for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does that impact the way in which you determined the identified -- the number of identified Srebrenica and Zepa-related victims?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. In no way. These columns, the first, I mean, I think five columns were the most important in order to determine which victims were found where and in order to determine the DNA connections between these victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we go over to the right a little bit more, and we see "Date of Disappearance," "Place of Disappearance," and then the type of report.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. For most of the cases, most of the entries, date of disappearance in this ICMP data will be 11 of July, because the purpose for their database was not to find out when and where exactly those individuals went missing, but the most important for them was to establish that they are somehow Srebrenica related, and then they designated 11 July for most of them. And also for the place of disappearance, it is the same issue. In order to get information on actual date of disappearance and place of disappearance, we have to look into a different source, which is ICRC missing list of these victims and also the OTP -- the OTP list of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So usually I'm not referring to these two columns when I'm looking to -- looking for information regarding when a certain individual went missing. I'm looking to different sources. And the last column, we see "Type of Report," which is also a very important column, because we can see two different entries. One is "Main Case," the other one is "Re-association."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could briefly tell us what the difference between those two designations are.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Main Case" can be -- and it is assigned to one individual only. So every individual which is identified gets only one main case. So -- and this same individual can get one or more re-associations. It means -- I'll explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means several -- because we have a lot of these secondary graves, and we know that these bodies, when they were reburied from primary graves, were disarticulated, and a lot of body parts have been found in these secondary graves. And most of those body parts have been tested and DNA samples have been found. And when several body parts were found for the same individual, so in order to exclude the possibility that we are counting one individual twice, they have assigned one main case for one individual. For the other body parts which were also found and assigned to that individual, re-association cases have been assigned. So it means type of -- if there is re-association, it means there must be at least one main case somewhere, and only one for one individual. And this is very important. When I was putting together the total numbers, the total number of the identified individuals from the Srebrenica and the Zepa, I counted only main cases, so in order to exclude the possibility that I would count one individual twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could just go to the next page. Make it a little bit smaller. Okay. If we could just blow this up a little bit on the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And then you can tell us what this page represents, in terms of your analysis.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is second page I prepared as a sample page in order to show my methodology, how I came up with the total numbers. So now, first, what I have made, I have sorted the actual spreadsheet by case ID. This is the fourth column. And now you can see the fourth column, "Case ID," is in alphabetical order. So -- and this is sample taken from somewhere at the beginning in order for you to see how it looks when you order it by case ID. And then when I ordered it like that, I have taken every single individual from this -- from this spreadsheet and placed it in a separate spreadsheet which were then related to a particular grave-site. For example, if you start with the first several entries, we see the case ID "BIS01SEK." This particular grave-site site code is related to the Bisina grave-site. So I've taken out of this spreadsheet every single individual which appears with this site code, and I placed all these individuals into a separate spreadsheet in order to get a separate -- a separate mass-graves-related spreadsheets. So -- and I have done the same exercise for all of the sites, so you can see different site codes down there, so towards the end of this spreadsheet are the ones related to Bljeceva. So I have done the same for every single entry there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to this particular page, I just wanted to direct you to a couple of things. First, we see an ID ICMP, or multiple ID ICMPs, I should say, for a couple of individuals here. If you look somewhere just below the middle of the page, you can see that. One is referenced as "5336" or "3387." And then below that, you can see another one which is referred to as "3106" or "3105." Do you see that in the middle of the page? Maybe we could blow it up a bit under the column --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's okay, I can see that. And this is what I have been talking about before. So here we have the sibling case where two brothers are possibly -- are most probably missing, and they cannot link -- they cannot say which of those two brothers was found in this particular place. So we can see then two ICMP IDs, and also under the first column you will see two names for both of two -- of these two brothers. And as I emphasised before, there is only one protocol ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what does that mean? Does that mean that only one DNA profile was found?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be the case that both -- both those brothers have been found, but the problem here we have, that in order to find that out, we would have to sort it by other way, and it means by the ICMP ID, and to see if both brothers -- if both brothers were found, there would be another case where we'll have the entry for both brothers, but the case ID -- not the case ID, but the protocol ID will be different. So if the protocol ID is different, then it means both brothers were identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say "identified," you mean that their profiles were recovered, or do you mean that they were actually identified by name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I referred as identified, it means -- based on these ICMP data, it means that they were matched to a donor -- donors' - yeah - samples. So it means -- it doesn't mean the actual final identification yet, because those information are then sent back to the pathologist, who, based on the anthropological examination of the body, decide -- decides if the body's complete and that it can be returned back to -- to the relatives, to the families.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to refer, if we could, a little bit -- if we could go a page up in this document and a little bit to the left. Yeah, that's pretty good. If we could go to the left a little bit more, that would be -- that's right. Now, with respect to the case ID, I can see two individuals here who appear to have similar, if not the same, case IDs, but they're different people, and I'm going to refer -- are we in closed session or private? Could we go into private session for a moment, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in -- we are in private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We are really running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And should we stop now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should, because another trial will use this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Yeah, this is a perfect place to stop, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have to adjourn now and to resume tomorrow morning in the same courtroom at 9.00. May I remind you, no contact to the parties about the content of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just wanted to add, for tomorrow, my understanding is that we'll continue with Mr. Janc until he concludes his direct testimony, which will be followed by Mr. Blaszczyk. And my understanding is that if Mr. Blaszczyk does not fill up the time for tomorrow, that Mr. Tolimir is prepared to proceed with the -- at least begin the cross-examination of Mr. Janc. Otherwise, he's prepared to proceed with the cross-examination of Mr. Janc after Mr. Erdemovic's appearance, if that's all right with the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If the parties are agreed on that, that would be very helpful. We can manage in that way so that you have enough time to prepare for your cross-examination. Thank you very much. We have to adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 9.00.
